claims.claim: GPT-6 Astra raised Qwen3.5-0.8B MATH-500 score from 7.9 percent to 48.1 percent by editing 0.016 percent of its weights.
claims.episode_span: In one experiment the team trained four identical-architecture networks on Breakout, Pong, Pac-Man and Freeway; GPT-6 Astra received only the 17,253 raw weights of each network and correctly named every game. A second set of tests used the same model to repair Qwen3.5-0.8B by changing 0.016 percent of its weights, raising MATH-500 from 7.9 percent to 48.1 percent, GSM8K from 13.8 percent to 67.1 percent, and IFEval from 21 percent to 62.3 percent.
claims.source_title: MIT Researchers Show LLMs Can Read and Edit Neural Network Weights Without Retraining
claims.supporting_quote: By modifying just 0.016% of the model’s weights, Astra increased its score on the MATH-500 benchmark from 7.9% to 48.1%.

claims.claim: AI-assisted pull requests at organizations tracked by LinearB are 2.6 times larger at the 75th percentile than unassisted ones.
claims.episode_span: Early users report that AI-assisted pull requests are now 2.6 times larger at the 75th percentile, yet review wait times have grown more than fivefold; the new effort-skill layer matches agent compute to change risk and business impact.
claims.source_title: LinearB Launches Agentic Studio to Help Engineering Leaders and AI Coding Agents Build Better Software Faster
claims.supporting_quote: LinearB’s 2026 AI benchmarks, covering 2.7 million pull requests across more than 250 organizations, show that developers who use AI most heavily nearly doubled their merged pull requests year over year. Yet the software factory faces new problems. In LinearB’s 2026 Software Engineering Benchmarks Report, AI-assisted pull requests were 2.6 times larger than unassisted ones at the 75th percentile, and agent pull requests waited more than five times longer for review.
